Carbon_Source: Traceable biogenic CO2 (for example, biogas upgrading or fermentation off-gas); source-specific quality to be verified
Hydrogen_Source: Renewable-electrolysis hydrogen intended to meet the Indian GH2 standard and GHCI
Hydrogen_Production_Configuration: ALK reference; PEM retained as flexibility configuration
Synthesis_Route: CO2 + 3H2 ⇌ CH3OH + H2O; catalytic CO2 hydrogenation; recycle/purge and crude methanol purification
Key_Unit_Operations: Biogenic CO2 recovery/conditioning/drying/compression; water treatment; electrolysis; H2 purification/drying/compression/buffer; O2 handling; mixing/preheat; synthesis/heat removal; cooling/condensation; gas-liquid separation; recycle/purge; distillation; storage; water/off-gas/waste treatment
Comparison_Control: Common methanol product boundary and product specification after design-basis approval; compare with A using same H2 configuration conceptually
India_Green_Methanol_Standard_Position: Directly aligned in principle: green H2 plus biogenic CO2 is expressly allowed; non-biogenic GHG ceiling 0.44 kg CO2e/kg MeOH over preceding 12 months; final MRV method must be checked
Primary_Advantages: Strongest biogenic-carbon narrative; direct alignment with notified carbon source category; international commercial-scale example
Primary_Limitations: Biogenic CO2 supply, continuity, quality and chain of custody unverified; substantial renewable electricity and water requirement; no Indian site data
Hard_Gates: Secure a continuous biogenic CO2 source; verify source origin/contaminants; renewable power evidence; water source; confirm current MNRE methanol MRV method
Status: Submitted for user approval; not approved or frozen

Carbon_Source: Existing industrial CO2 source; label its origin as fossil or biogenic based on source records
Hydrogen_Source: Renewable-electrolysis hydrogen intended to meet the Indian GH2 standard and GHCI
Hydrogen_Production_Configuration: ALK reference for controlled comparison; PEM may be evaluated as a flexibility subcase
Synthesis_Route: CO2 + 3H2 ⇌ CH3OH + H2O; same catalytic CO2 hydrogenation core as Route C
Key_Unit_Operations: Industrial CO2 source tie-in/capture or recovery; source-gas pre-treatment; CO2 drying/purification/compression; water treatment; electrolysis; H2 conditioning/storage; common synthesis, separation, recycle/purge, purification, storage and waste systems
Comparison_Control: Hold the downstream synthesis concept and electrolyser reference consistent with C to isolate carbon-source/capture differences
India_Green_Methanol_Standard_Position: Existing industrial CO2 is expressly listed as an eligible source in the 27-Feb-2026 Indian Green Methanol Standard; GH2 and 0.44 kg CO2e/kg MeOH non-biogenic threshold still apply. Fossil-origin carbon is not itself renewable.
Primary_Advantages: May offer an industrial CO2 interface near an existing source; same downstream loop as C; policy source category explicitly allowed
Primary_Limitations: Source capture, contaminants, continuity and capture energy are site-specific; fossil-origin carbon has different end-use/LCA implications from biogenic carbon
Hard_Gates: Identify industrial source; obtain source gas data and carbon origin; assess capture/conditioning duty later; establish carbon fate and threshold evidence
Status: Alternative for common comparison; not selected

Carbon_Source: Sustainably sourced biomass residues or eligible biogenic feedstock; sustainable surplus and provenance not yet proven
Hydrogen_Source: Hydrogen contained in biomass-derived syngas; GHCI explicitly lists biomass conversion including gasification as an eligible H2 pathway, but integrated syngas use needs certification-boundary clarification
Hydrogen_Production_Configuration: No electrolyser assumed in the reference route; an electrolyser/H2-trim branch must not be added unless separately justified
Synthesis_Route: CO + 2H2 ⇌ CH3OH; raw syngas gasification, cleanup and conditioning before catalytic synthesis
Key_Unit_Operations: Biomass receipt/storage/size reduction/drying; oxygen/steam supply; gasifier; ash/char separation; cooling; particulate/tar/sulphur/halide/nitrogen/trace-metal cleanup; composition conditioning; compression; methanol synthesis/heat removal; cooling/condensation; gas-liquid separation; recycle/purge; purification; storage; wastewater/off-gas/ash/char/spent-sorbent handling
Comparison_Control: Compare at the same methanol product boundary; do not force equal biomass/H2/power inputs because these are route outputs
India_Green_Methanol_Standard_Position: Biomass conversion is an eligible GH2 pathway under GHCI, but the Green Methanol Standard requires GH2. Direct use of mixed syngas is not presumed to meet separate H2 purification/compression/storage certification requirements.
Primary_Advantages: Potential use of agricultural residues and biogenic carbon; lower reliance on electrolytic electricity in a direct syngas reference; Indian biomass-to-syngas R&D evidence
Primary_Limitations: Gasification and extensive gas-cleaning burden; seasonal/competing-use feedstock risks; integrated biomass-to-methanol maturity lower; GH2 treatment in mixed syngas unresolved
Hard_Gates: Verify local sustainable biomass supply and quality; demonstrate catalyst-grade syngas cleaning; confirm GH2/Green Methanol standard interpretation for integrated syngas
